exposure: prenatal ultrasound scans (growth restriction, amniotic fluid index, Doppler results, early detected and long-lasting bowel dilatation)
maternal and fetal demographics (late presentation during pregnancy, gestational age at delivery)
outcome: unfavorable outcome (defined by more than 2 postnatal surgical interventions, intestinal resections, and long time to oral feeding (>=4 weeks))
cohort: The study included 23 pregnant women with a prenatal diagnosis of fetal gastroschisis at the University of Wuerzburg, Germany, between 1998 and 2011.
finding: Late presentation during pregnancy, earlier gestational age at delivery, and early onset as well as long duration of bowel dilatation are associated with a poor prognosis in neonates with gastroschisis, while other ultrasound characteristics like growth restriction, amniotic fluid index, or Doppler results are not predictive.
followup_time: At least 4 weeks after birth (for oral feeding outcome), with data collected from NICU and pediatric records.
